title: The pullback comparison of a commutative square
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\neq\ell$. Let $X,X^{\prime},Y,Y^{\prime}$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let all four arrows below be morphisms of $k$-schemes ([sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]). Fix a commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]), and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{\;g'\;} & X\\
{\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\
Y' & \xrightarrow{\;g\;} & Y
\end{array}
\qquad f\circ g'=g\circ f'
$$
be a commutative square. Write $c_{a,b}\colon L(b\circ a)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*\circ Lb^*$
for the composition isomorphisms of the restricted pullbacks on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
([def-sfb-dc-upper-star], [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp]). The *pullback comparison* of the square is
the natural isomorphism of functors $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X',\Lambda)$
$$
\theta_{sq}\colon Lf'^*\circ Lg^*\xrightarrow{\ c_{f',g}^{-1}\ }L(g\circ f')^*=L(f\circ g')^*\xrightarrow{\ c_{g',f}\ }Lg'^*\circ Lf^* .
$$
The middle equality uses only $g\circ f'=f\circ g'$. As a composite of natural isomorphisms,
$\theta_{sq}$ is a natural isomorphism.

proof.text: Use [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] and [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] to regard all four restricted pullbacks as functors between the displayed bounded constructible categories for the fixed commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$. The composites $g\circ f'$ and $f\circ g'$ are again morphisms of $k$-schemes between the same schemes, so [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp] applies to $(f',g)$ and $(g',f)$ with no additional coefficient hypothesis. It supplies natural isomorphisms $c_1=c_{f',g}:L(g\circ f')^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf'^*\circ Lg^*$ and $c_2=c_{g',f}:L(f\circ g')^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg'^*\circ Lf^*$. Both have source and target functors from $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)$ to $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X',\Lambda)$.

source.place: Definition: composition isomorphisms, commutative-square equality, and final natural-isomorphism sentence

proof.text: The hypothesis $g\circ f'=f\circ g'$ identifies the two scheme morphisms indexing the restricted functors of [def-sfb-dc-upper-star]. Substitution in this equality therefore gives an equality of functors $L(g\circ f')^*=L(f\circ g')^*$, on objects and morphisms. Let $e$ be its equality-induced natural isomorphism: after substituting one composite for the other, $e$ and its inverse are the identity natural transformation. This step uses only the commutativity equation, and does not require that the square be cartesian.

source.place: Definition: composition isomorphisms, commutative-square equality, and final natural-isomorphism sentence

proof.text: Put $A=Lf'^*\circ Lg^*$, $B=L(g\circ f')^*$, $C=L(f\circ g')^*$ and $D=Lg'^*\circ Lf^*$. Define $\theta_{sq}=c_2\circ e\circ c_1^{-1}:A\to D$ and componentwise $\psi=c_1\circ e^{-1}\circ c_2^{-1}:D\to A$. For a morphism $u:K\to L$ in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)$, the naturality equations of $c_2$, $e$, and $c_1^{-1}$ give $D(u)c_{2,K}e_Kc_{1,K}^{-1}=c_{2,L}C(u)e_Kc_{1,K}^{-1}=c_{2,L}e_LB(u)c_{1,K}^{-1}=c_{2,L}e_Lc_{1,L}^{-1}A(u)$. Hence $\theta_{sq}$ is natural. At each object, associativity and the inverse equations of the three factors give $\psi\theta_{sq}=c_1e^{-1}(c_2^{-1}c_2)ec_1^{-1}=c_1(e^{-1}e)c_1^{-1}=1_A$ and $\theta_{sq}\psi=c_2e(c_1^{-1}c_1)e^{-1}c_2^{-1}=c_2(ee^{-1})c_2^{-1}=1_D$. Multiplying the naturality equation $D(u)\theta_K=\theta_LA(u)$ on the left by $\psi_L$ and on the right by $\psi_K$ gives $\psi_LD(u)=A(u)\psi_K$, so $\psi$ is natural too. Thus the specified comparison is a natural isomorphism with the required orientation.

Recorded the required LeanFinder, Loogle, Mathlib grep, and LeanSearch queries; all found only generic or differently typed pullback comparisons. Wrote three elementary construction checks: type the two composition isomorphisms, obtain the equality-induced identity comparison by substitution, and explicitly compose natural transformations and their inverses. Added the direct condensed-ring definition dependency. Generic Iso.trans and eqToIso package the elementary operations but do not construct the project functors or their composition isomorphisms. The first server dry run rejected the imported opening in the setting of as non-self-contained (B2). Expanded it to the same prime, positive-characteristic field, distinct-prime condition, separated finite-type schemes and k-morphism hypotheses explicitly stated by sk-def-sfb-dc-setting. No hypothesis or mathematical content changed. Independent second reading expanded the final step into the component naturality calculation and both inverse equations; no change to the definition or its dependencies.

lean.statement:
noncomputable def boundedConstructiblePullbackSquareComparison (sq : CommSq g' f' f g) :
    boundedConstructibleUpperStar Λ ℓ g ⋙ boundedConstructibleUpperStar Λ ℓ f' ≅
      boundedConstructibleUpperStar Λ ℓ f ⋙ boundedConstructibleUpperStar Λ ℓ g'
lean.note: Exact existing definition in the published WeilConjectures framework, inspected through scompile.py --source (the local shared framework copy has an older explicit-k interface). Section parameters supply arbitrary commutative condensed coefficients, prime ell, a field of positive prime characteristic different from ell, separated finite-type Over (Spec k) objects and their over-morphisms. The body is (boundedConstructibleUpperStarComp Λ ℓ f' g).symm, then eqToIso induced by sq.w, then boundedConstructibleUpperStarComp Λ ℓ g' f, exactly the specified orientation and canonical formula. The comparison is defined before the IsFinitenessCoefficient section and imposes no cartesian, proper or coefficient-finiteness hypothesis. The branch label follows the dependency records for the published upstream root and its live/side overlay. No new module or definition.
